title: China’s AI Diplomacy Is Working
gist: Excerpt of a Foreign Affairs piece republished by CNAS: siloing U.S.-China AI safety cooperation from competition is fanciful; Beijing uses AI diplomacy to paint U.S. export controls as the obstacle and to court the developing world with an open, barrier-free Chinese AI ecosystem, and it is working as Chinese open-weight models spread.

insights.claim: The hope that U.S.-China cooperation on AI safety can be siloed from strategic competition is described as appealing but fanciful, since any AI-risk dialogue takes place inside the broader rivalry.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Don't expect safety dialogues to soften tech-control trajectories; competition dominates.
insights.quote: a belief as appealing as it is fanciful

insights.claim: To keep its lead and make progress on safety, the United States should treat AI dialogue with China as part of the competition rather than separate from it.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Implies U.S. policy will use dialogue tactically, keeping export controls as leverage.
insights.quote: If the United States wants to maintain its lead and make meaningful progress on safety, it needs to treat the dialogue as part of the competition with China.

insights.claim: The Biden administration paired sweeping technology restrictions with a narrow risk dialogue, while the Trump administration has kept a channel open even as it downplayed safety.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: U.S. AI policy oscillates across administrations, an inconsistency China exploits.

insights.claim: Unlike Washington, which has shifted its approach within and across administrations, Beijing has kept its AI diplomacy consistently focused on gaining competitive advantage over the United States.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Policy consistency is a Chinese strategic advantage in winning third-country alignment.
insights.locator: Beijing has long appreciated this dynamic

insights.claim: China has used international AI safety discussions and talks with the U.S. to portray U.S. export controls as the main obstacle to cooperation.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Diplomatic pressure on export controls may grow among non-aligned states.
insights.quote: to paint U.S. export controls as the main obstacle to cooperation
insights.locator: Beijing has long appreciated this dynamic

insights.claim: China casts itself as the champion of the developing world, offering a Chinese-led AI ecosystem without technological or financial barriers as an alternative to a restrictive U.S.-led AI order.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Global South AI-infrastructure and model adoption may tilt toward Chinese stacks, limiting U.S. vendors' TAM.
insights.locator: Beijing has long appreciated this dynamic

insights.claim: China's pitch is working: a growing number of states embrace its message and Chinese open-weight models are gaining users across the developing world.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Open-weight Chinese models are winning distribution share in emerging markets — a competitive threat to U.S. closed-model monetization abroad.
insights.quote: Chinese open-weight models are gaining users across the developing world
insights.locator: Beijing has long appreciated this dynamic
